乔治·拉塞尔以绝对优势夺得阿塞拜疆大奖赛杆位，而积分榜领先者基米·安东内利在Q1撞车，将从第16位发车。
拉塞尔在三节练习赛中状态极佳，并在Q3延续了强劲速度，以0.8秒优势击败法拉利的夏尔·勒克莱尔。
安东内利在Q1第一弯擦到内侧墙，尽管他努力继续并返回维修区，仍被要求在中段停车。

“所以是我的失误。非常不必要。说实话，我对此非常生气，明天会努力做得更好。”
这意味着当周六中午12点（10:30开始预热）灯光熄灭时，拉塞尔有很大机会大幅缩小与安东内利之间81分的差距，天空体育 F1和天空体育 Main Event直播。
“这可能是我整个职业生涯中最大的优势，甚至包括F2和F3时期，”拉塞尔说道，他自六月奥地利大奖赛以来还未获胜。

“这一圈感觉非常美妙。赛车整个周末感觉都很好，在这样的赛道上当你能够如此衔接时，感觉真的很棒。
基米·安东内利在阿塞拜疆大奖赛Q1撞墙
迈凯伦的奥斯卡·皮亚斯特里排位第三，这是他自七月底匈牙利大奖赛以来的最佳成绩，而红牛的伊萨克·哈贾尔在因手腕伤势缺席过去三个比赛周末后回归，位列第四。
马克斯·维斯塔潘看起来是拉塞尔杆位的真正威胁，但在Q3最后一轮飞驰圈中被兰多·诺里斯在第三弯锁死引发的黄旗所影响。
诺里斯仍将从第五位发车，但维斯塔潘仅排第八，落后于法拉利的刘易斯·汉密尔顿（第六）和阿尔派的皮埃尔·加斯利（第七）。
克雷格·斯莱特解析阿塞拜疆大奖赛，包括比赛为何在周六举行，同时尽力模仿克雷格·大卫！
威廉姆斯本赛季首次进入Q3，卡洛斯·塞恩斯排位第九，但这位西班牙人因在黄旗下未减速（当时他冲出赛道）被罚退五位，将从第14位发车。
凯迪拉克的塞尔吉奥·佩雷斯排位第20，但因在Q1阻挡皮亚斯特里被罚退三位，而阿斯顿·马丁的费尔南多·阿隆索和兰斯·斯特罗尔因更换新动力单元部件将从队尾发车。
拉塞尔充分利用安东内利的失误
拉塞尔在周四的两节练习赛中均排名第一，但周五上午的最后一节练习赛中，维斯塔潘排名第一，车手们差距缩小。
感觉梅赛德斯在进入排位赛时仍是热门，但优势不大，Q1和Q2也印证了这一点，拉塞尔在两节中均排名第一，但受到维斯塔潘的强力挑战。
由于缺少高速弯，除迈凯伦外，大多数车队在Q3全程使用同一套轮胎，以使其进入更好的工作窗口。
皮亚斯特里在第一轮飞驰圈后暂列杆位，随后拉塞尔快了半秒，并在最后一圈找到更多速度，做出不可撼动的1:42.526，无人能接近。
天空体育 F1的卡伦·昌多克与乔治·拉塞尔一起回顾他在阿塞拜疆大奖赛的杆位圈
勒克莱尔，这位四次巴库杆位得主，排位第二，但仍落后0.837秒，而皮亚斯特里和哈贾尔基本发挥了赛车潜力，进入第二排。
诺里斯推得太猛，在第三弯冲入缓冲区，这也影响了维斯塔潘的圈速，但拉塞尔的惊人速度即使对安东内利来说也难以击败。
“已经有一段时间了，所以感觉很好。这可能是我整个职业生涯中最大的优势，甚至包括F2和F3时期，”拉塞尔说道。
“这一圈感觉非常美妙。赛车整个周末感觉都很好，在这样的赛道上当你能够如此衔接时，感觉真的很棒。
“最后就是完美的一圈。我身后与哈贾尔有很好的差距，这让我在这条后直道上获得了大概零点一到零点二的尾流，所以很棒。”
detailEn: Azerbaijan GP: George Russell claims Baku pole from Charles Leclerc as Kimi Antonelli crashes in Q1

George Russell beat Charles Leclerc to pole position in Baku after championship leader Kimi Antonelli dramatically crashed in Q1 and will start 16th; watch the Azerbaijan GP on Saturday at 12pm with build-up from 10.30am, live on Sky Sports F1 and Main Event
Highlights from qualifying for the 2026 Azerbaijan Grand Prix
George Russell claimed a dominant pole position for the Azerbaijan Grand Prix as championship leader Kimi Antonelli crashed in Q1 and will start 16th.
Russell had been in superb form throughout the three practice sessions and continued his mighty speed in Q3 to beat Ferrari's Charles Leclerc by eighth tenths of a second.
Antonelli clipped the inside wall into Turn 1 in Q1 and was told to stop the car in the middle sector, despite his efforts to carry on and get back to the pit lane.

"I turned in and had a lot more front end compared to the lap before and I touched the wall," explained Antonelli, whose perfect Q3 appearance record in 2026 came to an end.
"So mistake from my side. Very unnecessary. To be fair, I'm very mad about it and will try to do better tomorrow."

It means Russell has a big opportunity to make significant inroads into his 81-point deficit to Antonelli when the lights go out on Saturday at 12pm (build-up from 10.30am), live on Sky Sports F1 and Sky Sports Main Event.
"It's probably the biggest margin of my whole career, even including F2 and F3 days," said Russell, who has not won since June's Austrian Grand Prix.

"The lap felt really sweet. The car has been feeling great this weekend and on a track like this when you can hook it up like that it feels really amazing.
Kimi Antonelli hits the wall during Q1 at the Azerbaijan GP

McLaren's Oscar Piastri qualified third, his best result since the Hungarian Grand Prix at the end of July, while Red Bull's Isack Hadjar was fourth on his return from a wrist injury, having missed the last three race weekends.
Max Verstappen looked to be a genuine pole threat to Russell but was caught out by yellow flags which Lando Norris caused after locking up into Turn 3 on the last Q3 runs.
Norris will still start fifth but Verstappen is only eighth, behind Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton in sixth and Alpine's Pierre Gasly in seventh.
Craig Slater breaks down the Azerbaijan Grand Prix, including why the race takes place on a Saturday, while doing his best Craig David impression!

Williams reached Q3 for the first time this season as Carlos Sainz qualified ninth, but the Spaniard received a five-grid place penalty for failing to slow under yellow flags when went off, and will start 14th.

Cadillac's Sergio Perez qualified 20th but was handed a three-grid place penalty for impeding Piastri in Q1, while Aston Martin's Fernando Alonso and Lance Stroll will start at the back due to taking on new power unit elements.
Russell takes full advantage of Antonelli mistake
Russell had topped both of Thursday's practice sessions but the field closed up in final practice on Friday morning with Verstappen topping the session.
It felt like Mercedes were still favourites going into qualifying, but not by a big margin, and Q1 and Q2 underlined that as Russell topped both segments but was being pushed hard by Verstappen.
Due to the lack of high-speed corners, most teams apart from McLaren unusually ran the same set of tyres for the whole of Q3 to bring them into a better operating window.

Piastri took provisional pole after the first runs before Russell went quicker by half a second, then found even more pace on his last flying lap to set an unbeatable 1:42.526 which nobody came close to threatening.
Sky Sports F1's Karun Chandhok is joined by George Russell to watch back his pole-setting lap for the Azerbaijan GP
Leclerc, a four-time Baku pole-sitter, qualified second but was still 0.837s behind while Piastri and Hadjar largely maximised what they had underneath them to get onto the second row.
Norris pushed too hard and went deep into the run-off area at Turn 3, which also compromised Verstappen's lap but Russell's remarkable speed would have been tough even for Antonelli to beat.
"It has been a while so definitely feels good. It's probably the biggest margin of my whole career, even including F2 and F3 days," said Russell.
"The lap felt really sweet. The car has been feeling great this weekend and on a track like this when you can hook it up like that it feels really amazing.
"It was just the perfect lap at the end. I was in a good gap behind to Hadjar, which gave me a nice little slipstream probably by another tenth or two down this backstraight, so it was great."

items.originalTitle: F1 Azerbaijan GP: George Russell takes dominant pole as Kimi Antonelli crashes out
items.summaryEn: Mercedes driver George Russell beat Charles Leclerc to take pole at the F1 Azerbaijan Grand Prix, while his team-mate and championship leader Kimi Antonelli crashed out in Q1 and will start no higher than 16th.
detailZh: F1阿塞拜疆大奖赛：乔治·拉塞尔夺杆位，基米·安东内利撞车出局
乔治·拉塞尔在F1阿塞拜疆大奖赛夺得他2026年的第五个杆位，而积分榜领跑者基米·安东内利撞墙后正赛最多只能从第16位起步。
梅赛德斯车手乔治·拉塞尔在F1阿塞拜疆大奖赛击败查尔斯·勒克莱尔夺得杆位，而队友、夺冠热门基米·安东内利在Q1撞车出局。
在6公里长的巴库城市赛道上，安东内利在Q1于1号左弯内侧撞上护墙，他的梅赛德斯W17赛车左前悬挂严重受损，无法驶回维修区。安东内利此前已做出足以晋级Q2的成绩，但已退出该节比赛，正赛最多只能从第16位起步。
队友拉塞尔在周四的练习赛中已展现出极快速度，他充分利用机会，力压查尔斯·勒克莱尔和奥斯卡·皮亚斯特里夺得杆位，这是这位英国车手本赛季的第五个杆位。
迈凯伦在Q3初段带来惊喜，皮亚斯特里和兰多·诺里斯在首轮排位冲刺中超越此前领先的拉塞尔。在经历了两节混乱的练习赛后，这支木瓜色车队尚未做出理想的排位圈，诺里斯甚至在Q1怀疑自己的赛车存在问题。
但皮亚斯特里1分43秒571的圈速对拉塞尔来说是可以超越的目标，这位英国车手在第二轮快了半秒，做出1分43秒037的飞快圈速，其他对手无人能给出回应。
在最后一轮冲刺中，拉塞尔又将自己此前的标杆提升了0.5秒，做出统治性的1分42秒526杆位圈。
法拉利采用了不同的冲刺计划，推迟了首轮出场，这让勒克莱尔暂列第二，这位摩纳哥车手又找到0.1秒，锁定发车格第二的位置，领先皮亚斯特里，但落后拉塞尔0.8秒，差距令人清醒。
伊萨克·哈贾尔伤愈复出后庆祝取得发车格第四，而诺里斯在最后一轮失误，最终位列第五，排在汉密尔顿之前。皮埃尔·加斯利为阿尔派拿下第七，马克斯·维斯塔潘疑似遭遇能量部署问题仅列第八，并在诺里斯引发的黄旗下进一步损失时间。
卡洛斯·塞恩斯充分利用威廉姆斯升级版FW48赛车取得第九，弗兰科·科拉平托在一节混乱的Q3后位列第十。
拉塞尔在Q2以1分43秒462的晚圈领跑，领先维斯塔潘0.2秒，预示着杆位争夺将十分激烈。
最后几个Q3席位的争夺是本赛季最激烈的一次，威廉姆斯也加入竞争，塞恩斯抓住机会升至第九，拿下难得的Q3席位。赛道状况的急剧演变意味着车手们需要携带多圈燃油，力争在最后一轮冲刺中达到巅峰。在最后时刻，阿尔派的科拉平托从哈斯车手奥利弗·贝尔曼手中抢走第十，与队友加斯利一同晋级下一节。
小红牛是Q2最大的受害者，利亚姆·劳森位列第12出局，随后是威廉姆斯的亚历克斯·阿尔本和哈斯的埃斯特班·奥康。阿维德·林德布拉德仅列第15，延续了这位英国车手迄今为止混乱的周末，此前他在FP2撞车，车队领队艾伦·珀曼将其归因于“新秀的热情”。
安东内利出局后，拉塞尔在Q1同样领跑，在节末以1分43秒615的圈速将维斯塔潘挤下榜首。与此同时，威廉姆斯两辆升级版赛车轻松晋级。
在一条暴露动力单元劣势的高速赛道上，奥迪为威廉姆斯的进步付出了代价，加布里埃尔·博托莱托和尼科·霍肯伯格分别位列第17和第18被淘汰。凯迪拉克和阿斯顿·马丁的四辆赛车也被淘汰，费尔南多·阿隆索和兰斯·斯特罗尔已因更换本田动力单元面临队尾发车处罚。
detailEn: F1 Azerbaijan GP: George Russell takes dominant pole as Kimi Antonelli crashes out
George Russell takes his fifth pole of 2026 at Formula 1's Azerbaijan Grand Prix while championship leader Kimi Antonelli won't start higher than 16th after hitting the wall.
Mercedes driver George Russell has beaten Charles Leclerc to take a dominant pole at F1's Azerbaijan GP, while team-mate and title favourite Kimi Antonelli crashed out of Q1.

At the 6km Baku City Circuit, Antonelli tagged the barriers on the inside of the Turn 1 left-hander during Q1, unable to limp back home in his Mercedes W17 with terminal front-left suspension damage. Antonelli had already set a time quick enough to advance to Q2, but was out of the session and is set to start 16th at best.

Team-mate Russell, who had already proven his rapid pace through Thursday's practice sessions, capitalised fully to take a dominant pole ahead of Charles Leclerc and Oscar Piastri, the Briton's fifth pole of the campaign.

McLaren sprung an early surprise in Q3 when Piastri and Lando Norris jumped early pacesetter Russell to top the first barrage of qualifying runs. Off the back of a messy brace of practices, the papaya squad had yet to string together optimal qualifying laps, with Norris even suspecting something was wrong in his car in Q1.

But Piastri's 1m43.571s lap proved an achievable target for Russell to beat, with the Briton going half a second faster on his second run to set a rapid 1m43.037s, which none of his competitors could find an answer for.
On the final run, Russell took yet another five-tenth chunk out of his own benchmark to set a dominant 1m42.526s pole lap.

Ferrari employed a different run plan by delaying its first run, which yielded Leclerc provisional second, and the Monegasque found another tenth that secured that position on the grid ahead of Piastri, albeit a sobering eight tenths behind Russell.

Isack Hadjar celebrated his return from injury with fourth on the grid, while Norris slipped up on his final attempt and settled for fifth ahead of Hamilton. Pierre Gasly secured seventh for Alpine as Max Verstappen could only manage eighth following a suspected energy deployment issue, and lost further time under a yellow flag caused by Norris.
Carlos Sainz made full use of Williams' upgraded FW48 to claim ninth, as Franco Colapinto qualified tenths following an erratic Q3 session.
Russell topped Q2 with a late 1m43.462s effort, two tenths ahead of Verstappen as it promised to set up a tight pole shoot-out.

The battle for the final Q3 spots was as close as it has been all season with Williams now in the hunt, and Sainz capitalised to go ninth and claim a rare Q3 berth. The dramatic rate of track evolution meant drivers were fueled up for multiple laps to try and peak on their final run In the dying seconds Alpine's Colapinto snatched 10th away from Haas driver Oliver Bearman, joining his team-mate Gasly in the next segment.

Racing Bulls was the biggest victim in Q2 with Liam Lawson out in 12th, followed by the second Williams of Alex Albon and Esteban Ocon in the remaining Haas. Arvid Lindblad could only muster 15th to continue what has been a messy weekend so far for the Briton, off the back of an FP2 crash which team principal Alan Permane ascribed to "rookie enthusiasm".

Russell also led the way in Q1 after Antonelli disappeared, demoting Verstappen at the end of the session with a 1m43.615s lap. In the background, Williams comfortably made it through with both of its upgraded cars.

On a high-speed track exposing its power unit deficit, Audi paid the price of Williams' progress as Gabriel Bortoleto and Nico Hulkenberg were both eliminated in 17th and 18th. The four cars from Cadillac and Aston Martin were also punched out, with Fernando Alonso and Lance Stroll already facing a back-of-the-grid penalty for Honda power unit changes.

拉塞尔最终圈速1分42秒526，比勒克莱尔快0.8秒，这是他本赛季第五个杆位。
维斯塔潘疑似遭遇能量部署问题仅列第八，塞恩斯驾驶升级版威廉姆斯赛车取得第九。
keyPointsEn: Antonelli hit the inside barrier at Turn 1 during Q1, suffering terminal front-left suspension damage that prevented him from returning to the pits, despite having already set a time quick enough for Q2.
Russell's final lap of 1m42.526s was eight tenths faster than Leclerc, marking his fifth pole of the season.
Verstappen could only manage eighth following a suspected energy deployment issue, while Sainz took ninth in Williams' upgraded car.
